result.title: SSM-Attack: Learning Where to Perturb for Black-Box Face Privacy
result.comment: 25 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables. Preprint submitted to Pattern Recognition
result.summary: Face recognition systems are deployed widely enough that a photograph shared online can be matched without its subject's consent. Generator-based protection methods rely on heavy pretrained backbones, multi-stage inference or visible semantic edits. We introduce SSM-Attack, a black-box face privacy framework built on Selective State Space Models. Rather than synthesizing the perturbation, the state-space model predicts in one linear-time pass a spatial allocation of the perturbation budget, marking which facial locations carry identity evidence; a short projected refinement then sets the values within this per-pixel budget. Against published benchmark results, SSM-Attack attains the highest average black-box attack success rate on all three evaluation sets: 87.10 percent on CelebA-HQ, 86.90 on LADN and 81.15 on FFHQ, the last from a network that never saw that dataset. The allocation network holds 5.73 million parameters, or 16.13 million with the frozen networks used by its quality terms. Under the same cap of 0.10 on the maximum per-pixel change, allocation improves structural similarity by 0.044, peak signal-to-noise ratio by 1.62 decibels and Frechet Inception Distance by 11.2 points over a uniform map while spending 37 percent of its capacity. Strong facial privacy protection therefore does not require a large generative prior; it requires knowing where to spend a small one.

AI.brief_summary: SSM-Attack 是一个基于选择性状态空间模型（SSM）的黑盒人脸隐私保护框架：不做生成式合成，而是用一次线性时间前向直接预测扰动预算在面部空间上的分配图，标出承载身份证据的位置，再由一个轻量投影细化确定具体取值。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心方法是用 SSM 单次前向预测「哪里值得投入预算」的空间重要性分配图，并强调小容量网络即可完成定位，这可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、LOOK 区域选择与计算预算分配提供可核查的方法线索；但原任务是对抗攻击与图像保真度优化，与内部推理状态的关系需人工判断，迁移性属推测。
